title: Simulation of a Custom-Made Temporomandibular Joint –an Academic View on an Industrial Workflow
content: Temporomandibular joint replacement is a critical intervention for severe temporomandibular joint disorders, enhancing pain levels, jaw function, and overall quality of life. In this study, we compare two finite element method-based simulation workflows from both academic and industrial perspectives, focusing on a patient-specific case involving a custom-made temporomandibular joint prosthesis. Using computed tomography data and computer-aided design data, we generated different 3D models and performed mechanical testing, including wear and static compression tests. The results demonstrate that the academic, retrospective, and purely image-based approach, applied post-operatively, yields biomechanical insights comparable to those derived from the industrial, pre-operative, planning-based process, which is additionally guided by regulatory requirements and approval protocols. Minor variations between the two workflows are primarily due to different assumptions, simplifications and constraints imposed by the regulatory framework. To elaborate the differences, various models were generated in the academic workflow, partly based on the data of the industrial process. These findings underscore the potential of patient-specific simulations not only to refine temporomandibular joint prosthesis design and enhance patient outcomes, but also to highlight the interplay between academic research methodologies and industrial standards in the development of medical devices.
